title: The nebula (NGC 6164/6165) surrounding HD 148937 as seen in visible light
caption: The Dragon's Egg nebula NGC 6164/6165 around HD 148937, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: HD 148937, NGC 6164, NGC 6165 · about 4000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A cloud of gas and dust surrounds a pair of stars in this image from the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory. The nebula is NGC 6164/6165, also called the Dragon's Egg, and the stars at its heart are known together as HD 148937.

Astronomers using ESO data found that the two stars are surprisingly unlike each other. One appears much younger than the other, and only that one is magnetic. The nebula, too, is significantly younger than either star, and it is made of gases normally found deep inside a star rather than on its surface.

Put together, those clues pointed to a solution. The system most likely once held three stars, until two of them collided and merged into a single new, larger, magnetic star. That violent event is thought to have thrown out the material that now forms the nebula surrounding the surviving pair.
scale: The source lists a distance of 4000 light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 4,000 years ago.

understand.summary: The image was taken in visible light with the VLT Survey Telescope. The source does not list the filters or publish the color mapping.
understand.eye: The long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye, revealing faint nebula gas that would be very hard to see directly.
